info.title: AXLR Bots domain events
info.description: The envelope of the domain events one team publishes to another (docs/architecture/team-topics.md). A domain event is a fact `<thing>.<what happened>` with the thing's id: it wakes the listening team and carries no instruction. Only the control plane publishes and reads these subjects: `axlr.domain.{tenant}.{team}.{name}`, where `name` is the event's own name. The platform names no event: an application (a separate repository, say) declares the events its teams publish and listen to in its own AsyncAPI, on this subject pattern and with this message. Idempotent: `Nats-Msg-Id` is the event's identity (sha256 of team, name and data.id), so the same fact published twice is one message within the stream's window, and the listener's task key repeats it. The wire form is `adapters/bus/domainevent.DTO`; the domain never sees it.

fleet.description: The fleet's NATS with JetStream; mutual TLS as in docs/architecture/bus-port.md. Stream AXLR_DOMAIN, subjects axlr.domain.>, file storage, a republish dropped within 2 minutes by Nats-Msg-Id.

domainEvent.title: A team's domain event
domainEvent.description: Every domain event a team publishes, under its own name. A listener of the team's events filters on `axlr.domain.{tenant}.{team}.>`.

publishDomainEvent.summary: The control plane publishes a bot's domain event to the teams its emit rule names.

receiveDomainEvent.summary: The control plane delivers it to the listening team's subscriptions (subscription team, deliver: team).

tenant.description: The tenant, with '.', '*', '>' and spaces written '_'.

team.description: The emitting team's memory name, written as the tenant is.

name.description: The event's name, `<thing>.<what happened>`, its own dots kept as tokens: segments of lowercase letters, digits and '-', of the info kind (never stop, danger, warn, error or done).

Nats-Msg-Id.description: The event's identity, the payload's id: JetStream drops a repeat.

id.description: The identity: evt- and sha256(team NUL name NUL data.id), 12 bytes in hex.

name.description: <thing>.<what happened>, of the info kind; never stop, danger, warn, error or done.

crossings.description: Team boundaries the trace crossed with this one; a fifth is refused (crossing_limit).

audience.description: The teams the emitter publishes this event to: the teams its emit rule names, never the emitting team. Not part of the identity.

id.description: The thing's id: an order, an item. A fact that can happen more than once to the same thing carries a round-specific id, so a later round is a new fact and not a repeat: <thing>@<round>, such as o-17@4f9c2ab.

context.description: The KMP key of the context (an about of the emitting team). The listener asks that team for it through the team channel; it never opens the other team's store.
